app.title: AxoDen: axonal density quantification from thresholded region images
app.summary: The person names a project, sets the pixel size for their objective, says whether the images are masked, and uploads a batch of .tif images whose filenames carry subject, region and group. Each image is analysed automatically: it is converted to grayscale, a threshold is set inside the tissue to split signal from background, and the image is binarised. The app then reports the percentage of signal pixels, the region area and the threshold for each image. The person checks per-image control plots grouped by region, reads summary bar charts and along-axis intensity profiles per region, and downloads the figures as PDFs and the tables as CSV.

task.text: Measure what fraction of each defined region in a batch of fluorescence images is covered by signal, summarise it per region with quality checks, and export figures and tables for statistics.

data.text: A batch of single-channel fluorescence images, each cropped to one region of interest, with subject, region and group parsed from the filename. These are reduced to a per-image table of pixel counts, areas and thresholds, plus per-image intensity profiles along two axes.
data.item: an image of one region of interest from one subject

stage.text: quantifying signal in prepared, masked region images, before running statistics

mechanism.text: An input form and an uploader run the threshold-and-count pipeline on every image as soon as files arrive, with a progress bar. Below it, a summary figure and table, an along-axis profile figure and table, and tabbed per-image control plots grouped by region each come with a PDF download. A separate desktop window runs the same pipeline on a folder and writes CSV and PDF files to an output folder.

field.text: threshold-based quantification of axonal projection density in fluorescence histology, in neuroscience

workflow.name: segment signal from background in a batch of images and summarise coverage per group

steps.here: enter a project name, set the pixel size in µm (defaults are given for 20x and 4x objectives), keep or clear the 'Images are masked' box, and drag in up to 100 .tif files named subjectID_brainregion_group

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: each image is converted to grayscale and given an Otsu threshold computed inside the tissue mask, then binarised; signal and background pixels are counted, converted to areas with the pixel size, and turned into percent innervation, with a progress bar per image

control plots are grouped in tabs by brain region, with a numbered sub-tab per image, each showing grayscale, binarised and mask panels with their axis projections and a pie of signal versus background, so the person can check the mask and look for signal bleeding

per brain region, bars show mean ± SEM with one dot per subject for percent innervation, region area and threshold, next to a list of the subjects and N in each region; the full per-image table is shown underneath
one row per brain region shows binarised signal summed along the medio-lateral and dorso-ventral axes, with each subject as a grey line and the mean ± SEM in blue

download the summary figure, the axis figure and all control plots joined into one file as PDFs that can be edited in Illustrator, and the tables as CSV from the table widgets; the desktop window writes the same CSVs and PDFs to an output folder

distinctive: The threshold is computed only over tissue pixels, because zero-valued pixels outside the hand-drawn mask are excluded, and it is set to 20 when Otsu returns 10 or less
Subject, region and group come only from the filename convention, and a filename with no underscore stops the analysis
Region area and binarisation threshold are plotted next to percent innervation as sanity checks, where low variance across subjects is the goal
Pixel size turns pixel counts into µm² and mm², with default values tied to specific microscope objectives
Signal is projected along the medio-lateral and dorso-ventral axes, and profiles of different lengths are padded so they can be averaged per region

parts.title: Summary Data Axis
